raw_text:
{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "fametrano",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "concerned tests lack nonce and BIP324 key isolation checks"
    },
    {
      "login": "vasild",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "finds reliance on DNS seeds and excluding Tor/I2P peers unacceptable"
    },
    {
      "login": "ajtowns",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "suggested implementing as a separate binary and publishing design as a BIP/mailing list post"
    },
    {
      "login": "darosior",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK"
    },
    {
      "login": "andrewtoth",
      "stance": "question",
      "note": "asked about addrman influence, I2P sybil attack vectors, and unresisted attacks"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:6397196009",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Tests do not verify that attempts use unique nonces and BIP324 keys, allowing regressions that let recipients link broadcasts to pass undetected.",
      "quote": "This PR's tests do not check that each attempt gets its own VERSION nonce, PING nonce and BIP324 key (A4 in `doc/design/private-broadcast.md`), so a regression there would pass.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author initially deferred but edited reply stating they changed their mind and brought it forward",
      "author_replies": ["c:6405247174"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6405247174",
      "status_by_quote": "changed my mind and brought it forward"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6413061893",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Relying permanently on centralized DNS seeds for each private broadcast creates a single point of failure and makes the feature vulnerable to outages or censorship.",
      "quote": "I do not think that it is reasonable to start relying on a few servers permanently (not just once in a lifetime, but every time a node wants to privately broadcast a transaction).",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied explaining seed downtime only stops broadcasts without leaking identity, whereas addrman introduces sybil leaks",
      "author_replies": ["c:6424580079"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6424580079",
      "status_by_quote": "If the seeds go offline, private broadcast stops; it doesn't leak."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6413061893",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Broadcasting exclusively to IP peers via Tor makes private broadcast fragile to Tor outages and exit node failures, lacking an I2P fallback.",
      "quote": "Only broadcasting to IP peers via the Tor network would make the feature too fragile - it would rely on the Tor network and the Tor exit nodes working properly.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied that Tor privacy outweighs its centralization and gathering addresses without seeder nodes reintroduces leaks",
      "author_replies": ["c:6424580079"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6424580079",
      "status_by_quote": "Tor isn't decentralized either, but we accept utility in terms of privacy."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6413061893",
      "part": 3,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Restricting broadcast recipients to IP peers degrades network-wide privacy by preventing Tor and I2P nodes from acting as indistinguishable recipients.",
      "quote": "Even moderate adoption of private broadcast in its current form improves the privacy of everybody because everybody could be a recipient. ... That would be spoiled if we only send to IP peers.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied that master's recipient model allows easy sybiling leading to IP leaks and offers limited attack resistance",
      "author_replies": ["c:6424580079"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6424580079",
      "status_by_quote": "The attacks it resists are quite limited today, and therefore it's sort of in purgatory where we can't make any promises"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4384957876",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Correct or remove misleading comment regarding protocol version tracking across releases",
      "quote": "70016 is what current private broadcast versions track, and avoiding varying these things across releases is exactly why we have a special profile.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author agreed the comment was bad and unnecessary and promised to change it",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4392392587"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4392392587",
      "status_by_quote": "yeah this is a bad comment and probably not needed, it should *not* update as a profile break which is what the static assert is for.... will change."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5662068682",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Publish the design as a BIP or post to the mailing list for broader discussion on design tradeoffs",
      "quote": "Shouldn't it be a BIP, or at least posted to the mailing list for broader discussion on exactly the sort of tradeoffs vasild raises above?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author agreed on value in wider discussion and noted the current implementation also bypassed the BIP process",
      "author_replies": ["c:6442248434"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6442248434",
      "status_by_quote": "I think there's definitely value increasing anonymity set if nothing else. By the same token, the current implementation should have gone through a BIP process, for exactly the same reasons."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5662068682",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Implement private broadcast as a separate binary interacting lightly with the node rather than in-process jobs",
      "quote": "If the idea is to separate this from the node, it seems like having a separate binary interacting lightly with the node might be a better structure.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied that they originally designed it as a separate tool but aimed for a like-for-like replacement in bitcoind, while noting the code structure supports separation",
      "author_replies": ["c:6442248434"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6442248434",
      "status_by_quote": "Originally I designed it as a separate tool, but I was hoping for a like-for-like replacement. However the architecture lends itself just fine to it, as the only coupled code in this PR to the node is the queue portion."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6446074543",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "How peers can be influenced into dialing fingerprinting peers, and whether that can be fixed upstream in addrman",
      "quote": "Can this design be expanded on about how they can be influenced, and why that is by design? Would this mean the problem is with the design that allows peers to be influenced into dialing to peers that are unique fingerprints, and not the actual private broadcast?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained addrman design goals differ and allowing peers to write to it enables fingerprinting",
      "author_replies": ["c:6449752844"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6449752844",
      "status_by_quote": "Addrman is built for partition resistance... private broadcast loses privacy to one dishonest peer that can \"read\" these differences."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6446074543",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "How an I2P sybil attack leaks a clearnet IP address, and how sybiling affects sending transactions through ephemeral I2P tunnels",
      "quote": "Would that be a problem with i2p in general, and not private broadcast? I'm not sure I understand how a sybil attack in i2p could leak a clearnet IP address.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained small I2P population facilitates sybiling recipient slots and correlating clearnet probes",
      "author_replies": ["c:6449752844"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6449752844",
      "status_by_quote": "The population of i2p is small, ... Once the attacker is a recipient, it can act on a suspect over clearnet before, during or after its private connection."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:6446074543",
      "part": 3,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "What specific attacks the current private broadcast implementation cannot resist",
      "quote": "Since we no longer make any promises, and this is marked experimental, can we elaborate on the attacks it cannot resist?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author enumerated past CVE-like fixes and detailed the active adversary model that correlates recipient slots to clearnet probes",
      "author_replies": ["c:6449752844"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:6449752844",
      "status_by_quote": "The fixes so far: #35032 (addrman updated from private connections), #35410 (v1 retry went over clearnet), #36277 (what recipients saw depended on receipt timing) and #36312 (discouragement of a private peer was observable)."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:6445520943",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Updated the record with comments from ajtowns, darosior, and andrewtoth, and author replies. ajtowns suggested an out-of-process binary and BIP/mailing list publication, and noted an inaccurate comment in params.h; andrewtoth asked clarifying questions about addrman fingerprinting, I2P sybil behavior, and attack resistance, which instagibbs answered; darosior left a Concept ACK.",
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "vasild, ajtowns, and andrewtoth to evaluate author explanations and replies",
      "id": "c:6449752844"
    },
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "push fix removing/correcting the params comment",
      "id": "rc:4392392587"
    }
  ]
}

claims.text: Tests do not verify that attempts use unique nonces and BIP324 keys, allowing regressions that let recipients link broadcasts to pass undetected.

claims.status_by_quote: The attacks it resists are quite limited today, and therefore it's sort of in purgatory where we can't make any promises

claims.text: Correct or remove misleading comment regarding protocol version tracking across releases
claims.quote: 70016 is what current private broadcast versions track, and avoiding varying these things across releases is exactly why we have a special profile.
claims.status_note: author agreed the comment was bad and unnecessary and promised to change it

claims.text: Publish the design as a BIP or post to the mailing list for broader discussion on design tradeoffs
claims.quote: Shouldn't it be a BIP, or at least posted to the mailing list for broader discussion on exactly the sort of tradeoffs vasild raises above?
claims.status_note: author agreed on value in wider discussion and noted the current implementation also bypassed the BIP process
claims.status_by_quote: I think there's definitely value increasing anonymity set if nothing else. By the same token, the current implementation should have gone through a BIP process, for exactly the same reasons.

claims.text: How an I2P sybil attack leaks a clearnet IP address, and how sybiling affects sending transactions through ephemeral I2P tunnels
